subtitle: Explode to leave the laboratory

body: 'Splosion Man is Twisted Pixel's Xbox Live Arcade platform game, released on 22 July 2009. A living experiment escapes through the Big Science laboratory by repeatedly detonating himself. The explosion is his jump, weapon and means of breaking obstacles, giving the player one central action with several uses. A room becomes a question about where and when that action should happen. The comic presentation makes the escape deliberately ridiculous, but the movement asks for careful timing as the player chains blasts through machinery and hazards that leave little space for a mistake.

Only three consecutive explosions are available before a cooldown, so a route must include a way to recover before continuing. The player uses walls, platforms and other objects to turn those limited actions into height or distance. An enemy can also become part of the route if exploding at the right moment removes it and carries the character onward. Repeated attempts reveal how a room is arranged. What first looks like a series of unrelated hazards gradually becomes one sequence whose movements need to connect without wasting the available blasts.

Separate multiplayer levels ask players to coordinate their explosions, turning timing into a shared problem rather than simply placing several people in the solo campaign. The game arrived during the 2009 Summer of Arcade promotion and was well received for the clarity of its idea and challenge. Xbox Live players selected it as their best original XBLA game that year. Ms. Splosion Man followed in 2011. The original demonstrates how much variation can come from a tightly limited verb when the surrounding rooms keep finding different reasons for the player to use it.
story_headings: Three blasts have to reach the next safe place
One action carries a cooperative challenge
